linkedin.title: Most news apps are designed to keep you scrolling, not to keep you informed.
linkedin.body:
It is a strange irony that the tools built to help us understand the world often leave us feeling more anxious and overwhelmed. The algorithm usually prioritizes engagement above everything else. That means loud, divisive, and endless streams of content designed to trigger a reaction rather than provide clarity.

We built Headlinne with a different philosophy. We believe AI should act as a filter, not a megaphone. Technology should help you cut through the noise to find the stories that actually matter to your life and your interests.

Instead of trying to capture your attention for as long as possible, we want to respect it. A smarter news experience is one that gets you what you need quickly and lets you get back to your day. It is about quality over quantity and relevance over rage.

We are curious to hear how you manage your own news consumption. Do you feel like you are getting better information, or just more of it?

story_card.headline: Scientists detect particles from Earth's core
story_card.standfirst: New measurements are helping us map the radioactive energy powering our planet.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: Detectors worldwide are tracking geoneutrinos. These are particles made deep underground.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: Researchers built a global network to capture these tiny signals from radioactive decay.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: These particles reveal the source of the heat that drives our planet's tectonic activity.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Scientists will use this data to build a clearer map of Earth's volatile interior.

story_card.caption:
Scientists are using geoneutrinos to map the interior of the Earth.

These subatomic particles are produced by the radioactive elements inside our planet. By tracking them, researchers can better understand the forces that drive tectonic movement. It is a major step forward in imaging the world beneath our feet.
